topic: structural tuning (deeper pipeline + double-buffered output) does not move the gated prefill ratio
change: prefill scheduling moved from rows=8/stages=2/output single-buffered to rows=2/stages=3/output double-buffered; decode keeps its certified configuration
screening: in one process, alternating with the vendor, the new scheduling screened ~12% better than the old one (0.727 vs 0.650 relative ratio), and output double buffering alone was ~4-8% better

comparison.conclusion: the candidate itself got faster (87.8 -> 81.4 us) but the vendor reading in the newer window was faster too (64.5 -> 59.6 us), so the gated ratio is unchanged within noise. No improvement is established.

lesson: single-process alternating screening overstated a +12% gain that the paired gated window does not reproduce. Screening may only rank hypotheses; the gate decides.
structural_bound_observation: for the candidate to reach parity its total must fall to roughly the vendor total (~60-70 us). Its DMA-in phase alone measured ~63-69 us and its vector work ~60 us, so parity needs both a faster DMA and better overlap - neither is delivered by scheduling parameters alone.
status: prefill remains ~0.75 and fails; decode EXCEED from R48 stands
